issues.body: `_fetch_dispatch_history` uses `json.loads(...).get("workflow_runs") or []` and then unconditionally returns an `ok` status. Thus a syntactically valid but invalid response such as `{}`, `{"message": "error"}`, or `{"workflow_runs": null}` becomes `([], {"outcome": "ok"})` and the public page says the fleet genuinely has no history. A non-list truthy value is also unsafe: a dict can raise at `runs[:count]`, while a string is sliced and silently reduced to no accepted rows before being marked `ok`. The new tests cover invalid JSON and a non-object root, but not this response-schema seam. Only an explicit list-valued `workflow_runs` field is evidence that history was fetched; missing or wrongly typed data must not license `fetched: true`.
issues.fix_hint: Validate that the decoded root is an object containing `workflow_runs` as a list before iterating. Return a failed/unparseable status for a missing, null, or non-list field, and add self-test cases (at minimum `{}` and a non-list `workflow_runs`) that assert they render as fetch failures rather than quiet history. Keep the explicit empty list as the successful quiet-fleet case.
issues.title: Malformed run-listing schemas are marked fetched successfully

verdict.summary: The new marker is wired through the generator and executed UI tests, but the fetcher still treats malformed successful responses as a successfully observed quiet fleet. That leaves the exact ambiguity this change is intended to close reachable at the response-schema seam.
